key_insight: ApexGO uses generative AI to redesign peptide antibiotics that more effectively kill drug‑resistant bacteria, with candidates validated in vitro and in mouse infection models showing equal or better performance than standard antibiotics.
problem_solved: Addresses the slow, costly process of discovering and optimizing peptide antibiotics against drug‑resistant pathogens by automating sequence design and prioritizing candidates for experimental testing.
method: Train and/or fine‑tune a generative model to propose novel peptide sequences conditioned on desired properties.
Score and optimize proposals using predictive models and constraint filters (antimicrobial activity, toxicity, stability), forming a design‑select loop.
Experimental validation of top candidates in laboratory assays (MIC, bactericidal tests) and in vivo mouse infection models to confirm efficacy.
impact: Demonstrates how generative models can accelerate biologically meaningful molecule design when coupled with predictive scoring and wet‑lab validation, providing a blueprint for applied AI in drug discovery and translational research.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: generative model → in silico scoring/filters → candidate selection → lab & mouse validation
Bar chart comparing MIC or bacterial kill rates: ApexGO candidates vs standard antibiotics
Sequence representation (logo or heatmap) highlighting designed mutations and property changes
Survival or bacterial load curve from mouse infection studies showing efficacy of top candidates
paper_title: A generative artificial intelligence approach for peptide antibiotic optimization
paper_authors: Marcelo D. T. Torres, Yimeng Zeng, Fangping Wan, Natalie Maus, Jacob Gardner
